How to use the builder

The builder runs locally and transmits no drawing data. Your work stays in this browser window until you save a project.

The window · Components · Connections · Selecting and arranging · Project values · Pages · Review · Saving and PDF · Tablets and phones · Shortcuts · Reference documents

The window

Bug Report beside Help opens an editable report with the application version and browser information. Describe the problem, expected behavior and steps to reproduce. Choose Open Email to address it to scott.finck@usda.gov, or Copy Report to paste it into webmail. If automatic copying is blocked, the report is selected for manual copying. Add screenshots or a saved project manually and review them before sending. The draft stays in this window until it is closed or reloaded.

The header displays the current NIICD logo alongside the project name and save status.

  • Ribbon. Commands are grouped on tabs.
    • Home: editing, tools, arranging and inserting. Save Project and Export PDF are available in File.
    • Insert: components by category, connections, fields and pages.
    • Arrange: alignment, distribution, position and layout.
    • Page: add, move and set up pages.
    • Project: project-wide values.
    • Review: warnings and reference documents.
    • View: zoom, panes, full screen and touch controls.
    Double-click a tab, or press Ctrl+F1, to collapse the ribbon; click a tab to show it again.
  • The heading shows CDO telephone, fax and email contact information. Telephone/email links open your configured calling or email application.
  • File opens New, Open, Save, Export PDF, project information, Help and About. Version history is inside About.
  • Quick access (top left): Save, Undo and Redo.
  • Components pane (left) and Format pane (right). Format shows the properties of whatever is selected, or the current page when nothing is selected. Its Review tab lists warnings. When a pane is closed, a tab on that side of the drawing shows it is there: tap the tab, or drag it inward, to open the pane. View → Show also shows or hides either pane.
  • Page tabs are below the drawing. The status bar shows the page, the selection, the number of warnings, the save state and the zoom.
  • 100% shows the page at actual size using standard browser sizing (96 CSS pixels per inch). Fit fits the whole page in the drawing workspace. Both buttons are beside the zoom menu in the status bar and phone command bar; they are also on View. Monitor scaling and browser zoom affect the physical size on your screen.
  • Right-click the drawing, a component, a path or a page tab for related commands. On a touch screen, press and hold.

Readability and dark mode

The interface follows your browser's default font size. Use your device's larger text setting where the browser supports it, or increase the browser's default font size. Controls and panes reflow; the drawing retains its paper dimensions. Use drawing zoom or Format to read and edit small drawing fields.

All connectors are solid. Type labels identify UHF and VHF paths as well as color, in both light and dark modes. Display labels are screen aids; saved labels stay as entered. Custom connectors are also solid in exported PDFs.

Dark mode in the title bar or View uses a charcoal workspace with light text, including the Components and Format side tabs, File navigation and dialog buttons. Choose Light mode to return. The preference is remembered when available; the paper keeps its drawing colors and PDFs are unchanged.

View → Page grid shows or hides full-inch dots with lighter half-inch dots inside the paper. Dots follow zoom and pan and never export or print. Grid visibility does not change the drawing or snapping.

Drag blank paper to box-select components. The temporary selection rectangle disappears when released or cancelled; selected components keep their outlines. Drag any side or corner of a secondary configuration boundary to resize it, or use Size (%) in Format. Escape cancels; Undo restores the prior size.

Size (%) scales the selected component proportionally; new components start at 100%. Components with fillable fields retain a 100% minimum to protect PDF readability; artwork-only items allow 60%, and boundaries retain their minimum dimensions. The maximum depends on the printable area. Undo restores a size change. Side/corner dragging remains available for configuration boundaries.

In Format, VHF/AM field boxes and text are red; UHF is blue. Fields are grouped in component order: VHF/AM first, UHF next, then shared fields. Tone fields use a single dropdown with NO TONE and the standard 16 tones; existing custom Tone/NAC values remain selectable. All channel fields offer CH 1–CH 16. Previously entered nonstandard channel values remain visible until changed.

Adding and editing components

  1. Start with File → New, or open a saved project.
  2. In the Components pane, search or browse the categories. Click a component to add it to the current page, or drag it onto the drawing. Insert → a category does the same from the ribbon.
  3. Select a component to move it or edit it in the Format pane: its Kit Number and Equipment Label (Site Context and Site Name for non-kit components), size and fillable fields. Drag on the paper to change position. Every visible title and field label can be changed. Add styled field adds an extra field.
  4. Enter latitude and longitude together in one field, latitude first, separated by a comma. On leaving the field, valid entries are formatted in the notation you entered: DD (45.50000° N, 120.25000° W), DDM (45° 30.000' N, 120° 15.000' W), or DMS (45° 30' 00.00" N, 120° 15' 00.00" W). Signs or N/S/E/W set the hemisphere; extra decimal precision is kept. Invalid entries remain unchanged with a warning. Existing saved values are not reformatted just by opening a project. PDF fields use the same formatter in viewers supporting JavaScript; other viewers may keep the entered text. Older project coordinates are combined when the project opens. Other legacy FCK and Repeater ID fields are removed; original 4150 battery and 4080 solar values are retained but hidden until enabled. Switch A CH and Switch B CH offer CH 1–CH 16; legacy switch values outside CH 1–CH 16 are cleared, so select the required channel.
  5. Optional 4150 battery fields. Select one supported kit and choose 4150 battery fields on Insert. The pressed button means on; click again to hide the fields. New kits and older projects default to off. Edit the added values in Format or on the drawing. Hiding preserves values in the saved project; hidden fields are excluded from the drawing and PDF. Undo/Redo, copy and duplicate preserve the setting and values. The kit grows vertically to fit the added fields at its existing size percentage and may shift to stay on the page.
  6. 4150 fields are available for all 4312 repeater variants, the UHF repeater (4248 template / 4244 kit label), 4281 cross-band, 4330, 4330EX and both 4370 configurations. There are two fields per kit, except 4330EX, which has one. The ribbon control is disabled for unsupported items or multiple selections.
  7. Optional 4080 solar panel field. Select a supported kit and choose 4080 solar field on Insert. It defaults to off and works independently of the 4150 toggle. The original single 4080-FCK field is available on all three 4312 variants, the UHF repeater, 4281, 4330 and both 4370 configurations; it was not present on 4330EX. The pressed button means on. Edit the value in Format or on the drawing. Hiding retains it in saved projects and excludes it from the drawing/PDF. Undo/Redo, copy and duplicate preserve the option and value. The kit gains space for either or both power-kit options without changing its size percentage.

Connections (paths)

  1. Choose a connection type (Home → Connection type, or Insert → Connection), then select the first and second components. Connect uses the current type. Press Escape to cancel.
  2. New paths begin straight and in front of components. Select a path to edit its label, arrows, controller, controlled element or drawing layer in the Format pane. Controller data does not change the visible arrow direction; set Arrows separately.
  3. Drag either small endpoint handle to move that end anywhere, including inside or away from its component; the endpoint follows the component when it moves. The Format pane also has buttons that move each endpoint without dragging.
  4. Use Add bend point only when a bend is needed, then drag the larger square handle. Corners round automatically, with a smaller radius for short bends. Straighten removes all bends.

Selecting, copying and arranging

  • Click a component to select it. Hold Ctrl (Command on macOS) or Shift to add components to the selection, or drag across empty page space to select everything inside the box. Ctrl+A selects every component on the page.
  • Cut, Copy and Paste (Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V) work across pages; connections between the copied components come too. Right-click empty page space and choose Paste here to place them at that point. Duplicate (Ctrl+D) copies in place.
  • Arrange aligns two or more components (left, center, right, top, middle, bottom) and distributes three or more with equal gaps. Auto layout gives the page a quick straight-path arrangement.
  • Arrow keys move the selection one unit; Shift+arrow moves ten. Arrange → Position moves it with buttons. Alignment guides and snapping are optional (Arrange or View); hold Alt while dragging to bypass them.

Project values

The Project tab holds the project name, incident and date shown on every page, plus two project-wide parameters.

  • Incident Tone. Select a tone, then press its Populate Fields button to set the VHF tone fields on all pages. New UHF tone fields default to T 1: 110.9 and remain individually editable.
  • Command Link Frequency. TX/RX are entered from the 4248 hub’s perspective and fill the opposite 4312 UHF RX/TX fields. Press its separate Populate Fields button to apply them. Blank frequencies leave existing values unchanged.
  • Changing a parameter or adding a component does not populate fields. Individual values remain editable; pressing Populate Fields again replaces manual values. Undo restores the previous values.

Filling in on the drawing. As in the PDF, Incident and Date can be typed straight into the drawing’s footer; tap or click the field. On a page with its own Incident or Date (Page setup), the footer changes that page only; otherwise it changes the value shown on every page.

Clear Form and Clear Page work on the drawing as they do in the PDF, and are also on the Project tab. Clear Form resets the fillable values on every page, including Incident and Date, to blank (tone fields to NO TONE). Clear Page does the same for the current page and its own Incident or Date, and leaves the Incident and Date shared by all pages. Labels, components and connections stay, and Undo restores the values.

Pages

Use the page tabs, or the Page tab of the ribbon, to add, duplicate, reorder or delete pages. Double-click a page tab, or choose Page → Page setup, to change the drawing title, page size, and page-specific Incident or Date. Ctrl+PageUp and Ctrl+PageDown move between pages.

Review warnings

The warnings count is in the status bar and on the Review tab of the Format pane. Warnings are advisory and never block export. Search or filter them, then select one to go to the page, item or field concerned (F8 goes to the next warning). Resolve unintended overlaps, invalid coordinates and unsupported PDF characters before export. No warning changes equipment or connections automatically.

Saving, opening and the PDF

  • Save project requests a download of the editable .niicd.json source and shows Download unverified. Cancelling or declining the download keeps unsaved-work protection. Choose Verify downloaded file in Project or File and select that file: matching contents show File verified. A stale or corrupt file preserves your drawing and explains the problem. Open project restores a saved file; an exported PDF cannot replace it.
  • PDF dropdown arrows are drawn by the viewer and have no supported width control. Their apparent size can remain fixed as the page zoom changes. Zoom in or enlarge the component with Size (%) if an arrow covers a value. The builder preserves native fillable dropdowns.
  • Export fillable PDF creates a separate form. Tone/NAC controls remain editable dropdowns, and Switch A CH and Switch B CH offer CH 1–CH 16. Adobe Acrobat Reader is authoritative for filling and saving, frequency and date formatting, and Clear Form/Clear Page; browser viewers may omit those enhancements.

Tablets and phones

When Format is closed, select equipment and use Edit fields beside the drawing, or select a connector and use Edit path. Zoom to selection makes small details easier to inspect; use Fit to return to the whole page. Closing Format returns keyboard focus to its edge tab.

  • On a touch screen, larger controls and path handles turn on automatically. View → Touch mode switches them on or off, and the setting is remembered.
  • Gestures.
    • Pinch the drawing to zoom; drag with two fingers to move around the page.
    • With one finger, Select moves equipment and path handles, and dragging across empty page space selects a group. Pan scrolls without moving anything.
    • Press and hold the drawing, a component, a path or a page tab for more commands.
    • Double-tap an item to open its properties.
    • After you rotate the device, the page refits.
  • Tablets. The ribbon is a single row, and the panes slide over the drawing from their own side; open them from the Components and Format tabs on the left and right edges. On a full-size iPad in landscape, both panes stay open. Tap a component in the Components pane to add it, or drag it sideways out of the pane onto the page. Multi-select lets you tap several components; turn it off to move the group.
  • Phones.
    • Components and Format slide in from the left and right edges; tap the tabs on those edges to open them. A command bar at the bottom has Select, Pan, Connect, Delete, zoom and the panes; ^ opens the ribbon as a sheet.
    • Tapping a component in Components adds it and closes the sheet, so the new item is selected in view.
    • Messages appear briefly above the command bar.
    • When the on-screen keyboard is open, the pane or sheet you are typing in ends just above it.
  • Save often. While you use another app, the browser can close the builder in the background without asking, and Safari on iPad and iPhone gives no warning before a page closes. Unsaved changes are then lost. The builder offers to save when changes have been unsaved for ten minutes (it waits until you pause), and when you come back to it with unsaved changes. It asks at most once every ten minutes.
  • Launching. The downloaded HTML needs a browser or approved local HTML runner that executes JavaScript and supports file selection and downloads. An iPad Files preview may not run the app; touch controls cannot change that operating-system limitation. Verify opening, saving, reopening the project and PDF export on your actual device before field use. No hosting is required.

About NIICD System Drawing Builder

Application
NIICD System Drawing Builder
Version
Release date
Supported browsers
Operating systems
Windows 10 and Windows 11. Optional tablet layout targets iPadOS and Android; local HTML launch, file handling, and device acceptance require verification (see Help).
Created by
Scott Finck, USFS Radio System Designer, scott.finck@usda.gov
Contributors
Bryan Stamps and Jose Lopez
Release status
Private internal production release; formal agency publication or approval is outside this package.
Data handling
Offline local-file application; it contains no network or analytics code and does not transmit drawing data.
Source graphics
Authorized NIICD System Diagrams V2026 and 2026 NIICD User's Guide extended-drawing artwork, bundled in this file for offline use.
PDF support
Adobe Acrobat Reader is authoritative for fill, save, clear buttons, and automatic frequency/date formatting. Browser PDF viewers provide basic fill and save.
Policy note
Managed browser policy must allow JavaScript in local HTML files. Internet Explorer is not supported.

2.0.3 · October 12, 2026

2.0.2 · October 12, 2026

  • Version history is available in About; its separate File entry is removed.

2.0.1 · October 12, 2026

  • Format groups VHF/AM fields in component order, then UHF fields, then shared fields. Tone values use one dropdown, retaining existing custom values.
  • Field label/value boxes align horizontally; Kit Number and Equipment Label are bold.
  • Size (%) replaces X, Y, Width and Height for all components. New components start at 100%; resizing preserves proportions and enforces PDF-safe minimums and printable-area limits.

2.0.0 · October 13, 2026

  • The selection rectangle disappears immediately on release or cancellation; selected components remain ready to move.
  • View → Page grid toggles measuring dots inside the paper. The workspace stays clear and grids never appear in exported PDFs.
  • Drag any side or corner of a secondary configuration boundary to resize it; Undo and cancellation restore the previous size.

  • Format shows VHF/AM inputs in red and UHF inputs in blue, with all standard tone choices and CH 1 through CH 16 dropdowns. Custom Tone/NAC text remains editable.
  • Dark mode replaces red night mode with a charcoal workspace and readable light text; paper and exports retain their drawing colors.
  • Application files now use NIICD_System_Drawing_Vx.x.x.html, derived from release metadata. Help and version history describe the current release.

B2.2026.10.12.1 · October 12, 2026

  • Save shows Download unverified until Verify downloaded file confirms that the downloaded project matches the current drawing. Cancelled downloads and stale files keep unsaved-work protection; verification keeps the drawing and undo history.
  • Help and File contain keyboard focus and prevent shortcuts from changing the drawing behind them. F1 opens Help; Ctrl+F1 collapses the ribbon. Closing a pane returns focus to its control.
  • A compact tablet ribbon keeps a consistent height across tabs. Selection actions expose Edit fields, Edit path and Zoom to selection while Format is closed; Fit stays reachable on small screens.
  • 100% and Fit have separate controls. Actual size uses browser paper sizing and a distinct 1:1 icon; Fit brings every page edge back into view after panning, including wide paper on phones.
  • Prominent full-inch dots, muted half-inch dots and numbered top and left inch rulers follow zoom and pan. They are display aids and are absent from saved projects and PDFs.
  • Solid connectors use rounded bends. Zoom and drag updates stay responsive, with clearer component icons, larger preferred text support and red night-mode controls.
  • Tablet and phone save reminders appear after ten minutes of unsaved changes at a pause, or when returning to the builder. Downloading keeps the reminders active until the file is verified.
  • About, File and this history share the same release identity and date. The primary edition has automated browser, accessibility and project/PDF compatibility checks.
